info.title: join-api
info.description: Integrate your recruiting tools with JOIN. Manage jobs and applications, read candidate profiles and interview scorecards, and maintain company locations. Requests use company API tokens and the `/v3` base path; select a dated revision with the `Join-Version` header.

tags.name: Applications
tags.description: An application connects a candidate to a job. Read applications, create one for a new or existing candidate, store your external reference, and move an application through the job’s hiring stages.

post.description:
Creates an application on a job. Provide `jobId` and exactly one of `candidateId` or `candidate`.

**Choosing a candidate**

- Use `candidateId` for a candidate already in your company.
- Use `candidate` to provide inline details. If the email matches an existing candidate, JOIN reuses that candidate, applies new tags and ignores the other supplied profile fields.

**Initial state and documents**

New applications start as `ACTIVE` in the job’s first review stage. JOIN sets their source. When `documents` is omitted for an existing candidate, their profile CV and cover letter are carried forward automatically.

Follow the [application workflow](applications-workflow), then [move the application to a stage](updateapplicationstage).

get.description:
Returns your company’s applications as a paginated list.

- Results are ordered by creation date, oldest first unless `sort` requests newest first.
- Filters combine with AND. No matches returns an empty list.
- Applications deleted in JOIN are excluded.
- Follow `nextCursor` until it is `null`.

See [Pagination, filtering and sorting](pagination) for shared conventions.

put.description:
Moves an application to a stage of its job. Read the job’s `stages` and send the chosen `stageId`.

**Effects of a move**

- The target stage can schedule automated emails, just as a recruiter’s move in JOIN does.
- Moving to a `HIRED` stage hires the candidate.
- Moving to the current stage makes no change.
- Rejected applications cannot be moved.

See [Get a job](getjob) to find stage IDs and [Responses, errors and retries](requests-and-responses) before retrying a move.

get.description:
Returns your company’s candidates, each with their application summaries. Archived candidates are included; deleted candidates are excluded.

**Listing and searching**

- Without `q`, results use creation order: oldest first by default, or newest first with `sort`.
- With `q`, results use relevance order. Do not send `sort` with `q`; this returns `filter_invalid`.
- A cursor belongs to its original ordering. Do not reuse it when switching between a search and a creation-ordered list.
- Filters combine with AND. No matches returns an empty list. Follow `nextCursor` until it is `null`.

See [Pagination, filtering and sorting](pagination) for shared conventions.

- Content is limited to 2,500 characters and cannot be edited after creation.
- A candidate with 50 or more notes cannot receive a new note (`note_limit_reached`). Delete an existing note before adding another.

post.description:
Creates and publishes a job. Provide its title, description, work location and contract type.

**Publishing effects**

- `ONLINE` posts the job to job boards.
- `OFFLINE` keeps it internal for direct sourcing and internal hiring, without multiposting.
- Both statuses run publish validation and count toward your company’s active-job limit.

Choose IDs from the Locations, Contract types, Pipeline templates and Remote regions endpoints as needed. Employment type follows from the contract type.

See the [job workflow](create-and-manage-jobs) for choosing these values and [Update a job](updatejob) for later changes.

patch.description:
Updates a published job’s details, status, or both.

**Updating fields**

- Omitted fields stay unchanged. Send `null` only for fields documented as nullable.
- Provided work locations, compensation, application forms and hiring-team arrays replace their previous values in full. Read each field’s rules before sending a partial object.
- Employment terms have their own field-level rules; see `employmentTerms`.

**Saving changes and handling failures**

Job fields, hiring-team assignments and status are saved together. If a status transition is refused, those changes stay unapplied. Custom screening questions are updated separately before that save and can remain changed if a later step fails. Read the job, including its application form, before deciding what to retry. If updates overlap, the last write determines the stored values.

See [Responses, errors and retries](requests-and-responses) for handling an uncertain write outcome.

post.description:
Creates a location. Provide an `address` with `countryCode` and `city`; the location name, street details and postal code are optional. The postal code is validated against its country.

Use `establishmentId` where an official establishment number applies, such as SIRET in France. Setting `isDefault: true` makes this location the company default and removes that designation from the previous default.

See [Update a location](updatelocation) for subsequent changes.

BearerAuth.description: Company API token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Every endpoint requires it. A missing header is rejected with 401 `authentication_required`; a malformed, unknown or revoked token — or a token whose company no longer has API access — is rejected with 401 `token_invalid`.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description: Preferred language for translated display names. Supported languages are en, de, fr, es, it and nl. Regional variants use their main language (de-CH → de); a list uses the first supported language. If the header is omitted or no language matches, the response uses English. Content-Language identifies the language used. Identifiers, slugs and enum values stay stable. Use languageCode to filter jobs by the language of the ad.

CreationSort.name: sort
CreationSort.description: Order by creation date: `createdAt` for oldest first, the default, or `-createdAt` for newest first. A cursor keeps the order it was read under

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Position from the previous response's `nextCursor`. Omit on the first request

JoinVersion.name: Join-Version
JoinVersion.description: Selects a dated API revision in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, such as `2026-11-01`. Pin this header to choose the revision explicitly; omitting it uses the server’s default. An unsupported value returns `400 unsupported_api_version`. See [Versions and compatibility](versioning-and-depreciation).

Deprecation.description: Set only when the resolved API version is deprecated: when the version was deprecated, as a Unix timestamp prefixed with `@`. See RFC 9745.

Link.description: Set only when the resolved API version is deprecated: a link to the migration guide, with `rel="sunset"`.

RateLimitBurstLimit.description: Burst request quota: the maximum number of requests allowed per token in the short burst window (currently 100 requests / 10s).

RateLimitBurstRemaining.description: Requests left in the current burst window for this token.

RateLimitBurstReset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the burst window resets.

RateLimitLimit.description: Sustained request quota: the maximum number of requests allowed per token in the sustained window (currently 600 requests / 60s). Present on every response served past authentication.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current sustained window for this token.

RateLimitReset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at which the sustained window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Sent only on 429 responses.

Sunset.description: Set only when the resolved API version is deprecated: an HTTP date after which the version stops being served. See RFC 8594.

WorkLocation.description: Where the job is performed. Which of the optional members is set follows from `workplaceType` and `remoteType`: `location` for `ONSITE`/`HYBRID`, `hybridSchedule` for `HYBRID` when one is set, `countryCode` for `REMOTE` + `COUNTRY`, `remoteRegion` for `REMOTE` + `REGION`, and none of them for `REMOTE` + `ANYWHERE`.

WorkLocationInput.description: Where the job is performed. Each workplace model carries exactly the fields it needs and refuses the others: `locationId` for `ONSITE` and `HYBRID`, `hybridSchedule` optionally for `HYBRID`, and then `countryCode` for `REMOTE` + `COUNTRY` or `remoteRegionId` for `REMOTE` + `REGION`. `REMOTE` + `ANYWHERE` carries none of them. Replaced in full on update, so changing the model clears what the previous one carried.
